scenes.dialogue: A State changes how garbage is handled in one hundred and forty seven urban centres. A court stays the whole plan. Should a court freeze public sanitation like that?

scenes.chip: 1 · A STAY ON THE WASTE PLAN

scenes.dialogue: Private waste operators called the plan arbitrary, and a Madras High Court judge stayed all of it. Can the State appeal that interim stay? And will the stay survive?
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. In Madras, Honourable Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Honourable Justice G Arul Murugan ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. In Madras, Honourable Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Honourable Justice G. Arul Murugan ruled.

scenes.dialogue: On ninth October, Tamil Nadu issued a Government Order restructuring solid waste management in one hundred and forty seven urban local bodies.
scenes.shown: On 9 October, Tamil Nadu issued a Government Order restructuring solid waste management in 147 urban local bodies.

scenes.dialogue: An association of waste operators challenged it in a writ petition. On thirtieth October, a Single Judge stayed the whole order, and the State appealed.
scenes.shown: An association of waste operators challenged it in a writ petition. On 30 October, a Single Judge stayed the whole order, and the State appealed.

scenes.dialogue: The State said waste policy is the executive's call, contractors have no right to endless renewals, and a blanket stay risked sanitation paralysis.
The operators said the two categories had no rational basis, and they had invested in trucks. They said the State should first ask the Single Judge to lift the stay.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? This was no routine order. It froze sanitation across one hundred and forty seven urban centres, so an appeal lay.

scenes.dialogue: Against overwhelming public interest, private commercial expectations must yield. The balance favoured the State, so the stay was set aside; the main case continues.
